Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Unity Insurance Group Inc. Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Unity Insurance Group's Second Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Unity Insurance Group's performance for the second quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust reinsurance recoveries, disciplined asset allocation, an improved combined ratio across segments, enhanced investment income yields, and strategic management of realized and unrealized gains on our portfolio. Our focus on profitable growth and advanced risk management continues to yield positive outcomes.

David, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

David Chen: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $250 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong reinsurance inflows, optimized investment returns, and underwriting discipline. Our combined ratio was 92.4%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. Investment income for the quarter was $285 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with an RBC ratio of 520%.

Before I dive deeper into the segment results, I'd like to spend some time on a critical component of our P&C underwriting performance: reinsurance recoveries received and expected. As you know, our reinsurance program is a cornerstone of our risk management strategy, allowing us to maintain disciplined net loss ratios while pursuing attractive gross writings in high-return lines like specialty casualty and property catastrophe. In the second quarter, we saw robust recovery activity driven by the 2023 North Atlantic hurricane season's tailwinds, particularly from Hurricane Idalia and the California wildfires, which continue to unwind through our excess-of-loss towers.

Let me start with the numbers. For the first half of 2024, we recognized $285 million in reinsurance recoveries received, up 42% from $201 million in the first half of 2023. This includes $162 million in cash collections in Q2 alone, reflecting accelerated billing cycles on our 2023 catastrophe events. On a gross loss basis, these recoveries represented 68% cession on our $420 million in paid cat losses year-to-date – a strong capture rate compared to our targeted 65-70% net retention. Breaking it down by layer: our first-event quota share with Swiss Re covered 30% of the initial $150 million layer, yielding $45 million received; while our XOL towers with Munich Re and RenaissanceRe kicked in above that, delivering $120 million on clashes from multi-peril events.

Looking at the balance sheet, our gross reinsurance recoverables stood at $1.2 billion as of June 30th, net of $875 million after uncollectible provisions and collateral offsets. Of this, $450 million is current – expected to convert to cash within the next 12 months – with 85% collateralized via trusts and letters of credit from our A-rated panel. We maintain a conservative allowance for uncollectible recoverables at 3.2% of gross, down from 4.1% last year, thanks to our enhanced cedant audits and the implementation of our proprietary ReClaim AI platform, which uses machine learning to predict recovery timelines based on historical bordereaux data from peers like Chubb and Travelers.

Shifting to expected recoveries: our actuaries project an additional $380-420 million in ultimate recoverables for 2023 events alone, with $290 million anticipated in the second half of 2024. This is underpinned by favorable prior year development on our $2.8 billion gross ultimate for Idalia and the Woolsey Fire analog events, where IBNR has stabilized at $180 million after refreshing our RMS v18.1 cat models. For context, our net paid loss ratio improved by 520 points sequentially due to these inflows, helping us deliver a calendar year combined ratio of 92.4% in Q2 – our best in three years.

Regionally, North America drove 72% of year-to-date receipts, primarily from Florida windstorm deductibles under our 2% fan deductible structure with PartnerRe. We've seen healthy billings here, with 95% recovery on gross paid within 90 days, aided by Florida's streamlined OIR mediation processes. In EMEA, recoveries from Storm Ciarán totaled $38 million received, or 55% of gross, but we're monitoring slower collections from our proportional treaties with Scor SE amid UK flood litigation backlogs – expect $25 million more in Q3. Asia-Pacific contributed $22 million, mainly typhoon recoveries via our sidecar with Korean Re, though rising reinsurance pricing in Japan, up 15% at renewal, has us optimizing our catastrophe bond issuances, including our $150 million UnityCat 2024-I notes placed in June at a 4.75% coupon.

Strategically, we're not resting on these laurels. Post the January 1 renewals – where we secured a 12% reduction in cat pricing despite a hardening market – we've diversified our panel to include emerging capacity from Third Point Re and Fermat Capital, reducing single-name concentration from 22% to 14%. We've also launched technical initiatives like automated bordereaux reconciliation with our reinsurers using blockchain pilots with Lloyd's of London, cutting disputes by 30% and accelerating cash by 45 days. On the modeling front, we're migrating to AIR Worldwide's Touchstone platform for real-time peril analytics, which flagged a $50 million uplift in wildfire recoverables during Q2.

Looking forward, we expect full-year 2024 reinsurance recoveries of $650-700 million, implying $420 million received and $230-280 million added to recoverables. This assumes normalized cat activity – secondary perils like severe convective storms at 110% of 10-year average – and no major disputes. Sensitivities include inflation pass-through on liability lines, where we've invoked 8% indexation clauses in 60% of our casualty XOL contracts, potentially adding $40 million. On capital, these inflows bolster our RBC ratio to 520%, giving us dry powder for opportunistic M&A like our recent bolt-on acquisition of Midwest regional carrier assets.

In summary, our reinsurance recoveries underscore the resilience of our program: high-quality cedings, proactive collections, and forward-looking analytics driving earnings stability. We're well-positioned in a market where reinsurers like Berkshire Hathaway Re are tightening terms, but our relationships and data edge keep us ahead.

As we continue into the financials, I'd like to provide a comprehensive overview of our asset allocation strategy, which remains the cornerstone of our asset-liability management—or ALM—framework at Unity Insurance Group. With $450 billion in general account invested assets as of June 30th, our portfolio is designed to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns while ensuring robust liability matching, capital efficiency under Solvency II and NAIC frameworks, and resilience against macroeconomic volatility.

Our allocation philosophy is rooted in three pillars: liability-driven investing to mitigate interest rate and longevity risks; yield enhancement through selective credit and illiquid exposures; and portfolio diversification to navigate the current high-inflation, rising-rate environment. We've maintained a conservative stance amid the Fed's terminal rate around 5.25-5.50%, widening credit spreads—now at 110bps for IG corporates per Bloomberg—and persistent geopolitical tensions impacting energy and EM markets.

Fixed income continues to dominate, comprising 72% of our portfolio, or $324 billion, down slightly from 75% at year-end 2023 as we tactically rotated into higher-returning alternatives. This segment generated a 4.2% year-to-date total return, outperforming the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate by 80bps, driven by our overweight in intermediate-duration corporates and RMBS. Breakdown: investment-grade corporates at 42% ($136 billion), U.S. Treasuries and agencies at 18% ($58 billion), MBS/ABS at 15% ($49 billion), and municipals at 8% ($26 billion). High-yield remains capped at 4% ($13 billion) for yield pickup without excessive credit risk.

Effective duration stands at 6.2 years, closely aligned with our $380 billion in policyholder liabilities (duration 6.5 years), supported by interest rate swaps totaling $50 billion notional to extend duration amid the yield curve inversion. Our LDI overlay has kept our economic capital charge stable at 15% of RBC. Book yield compressed to 4.8% from 5.1% year-over-year due to reinvestment at lower intermediate yields post-March rally, but new-money yields improved to 5.3% on 10-year Treasuries. Credit migration has been minimal—only 20bps deterioration in our internal ratings—with non-accruals under 0.5%.

Regionally for fixed income: U.S. exposure is 65% ($211 billion), focused on financials like the banking sector post-SVB stress tests and utilities for inflation protection. Europe at 20% ($65 billion) emphasizes Eurozone sovereigns and covered bonds, benefiting from ECB's hawkish pause; yields here are 3.9% versus 4.6% U.S. Asia-Pacific at 15% ($48 billion) tilts to JGBs and AUD corporates, hedging yen carry trades. We've launched an AI-driven credit surveillance platform, partnering with BlackRock's Aladdin, to monitor 15,000+ issuers in real-time, reducing downgrade surprises by 30%. ESG integration now covers 60% of IG holdings, targeting SFDR Article 8/9 compliance for our European book. Strategically, we're de-risking by ladder-maturing $40 billion in legacy holdings into LMIA for tax efficiency.

Equities represent 15%, or $67.5 billion, up from 12% year-over-year, reflecting our view on earnings resilience amid soft-landing scenarios. Year-to-date return of 11.5% beat the S&P 500's 10.2%, with low-beta strategies minimizing volatility. Breakdown: public equities 10% ($45 billion)—60% U.S. large-cap (tech and healthcare overweight), 25% Europe (STOXX 600), 15% Asia (MSCI Japan). Preferreds and convertibles at 5% ($22.5 billion) for hybrid income. Dividend yield of 2.8% supports our DA models, with buybacks providing tailwinds. Volatility, realized at 12%, is managed via VIX futures overlays.

Regional for equities: U.S. dominates at 70% ($47 billion), with positions in dividend aristocrats like Procter & Gamble and JPMorgan for stability. Europe (20%, $13.5 billion) favors defensives like Nestlé amid deglobalization risks. Asia (10%, $7 billion) includes Taiwan semis, but we're underweight China due to property sector woes. Enhanced quantitative screens via our proprietary factor model—value, quality, low-vol—have boosted alpha by 150bps. We're piloting a 2% ($900 million) allocation to UCITS ETFs for liquidity. This bucket enhances growth for our variable annuity and whole life products, where equity backing ratios average 105%—well above regulatory minimums.

Alternatives at 13%, or $58.5 billion (up from 9% year-over-year), are our yield engine, targeting 7-9% IRRs to combat liability compression from longevity improvements. Vintage diversification (2018-2024) and 40% dry powder mitigate J-curve effects. Breakdown: private credit 5% ($22.5 billion, 8.2% blended yield), real assets (REITs/infrastructure) 4% ($18 billion), private equity 3% ($13.5 billion), and hedge funds 1% ($4.5 billion). Performance: 9.1% annualized net IRR since inception, with private credit's senior loans (SOFR + 450bps) shining in a floating-rate world. Infrastructure returned 10.2% on inflation-linkers.

Trends: illiquidity premium widened to 300bps amid bank retrenchment post-SVB, enabling us to deploy $8 billion year-to-date. PE multiples compressed to 11x EBITDA, favoring secondaries. Regional: North America 55% ($32 billion), Europe 30% ($18 billion)—core+ office in London/Frankfurt—and Asia 15% ($8.5 billion), focused on Indian infra via GP stakes like Brookfield. EM exposure tightly gated at 2% total. Initiatives: our $5 billion evergreen private credit fund-of-one with Ares Management targets middle-market direct lending, achieving 95% advance rates. We've adopted RPA for GP due diligence, cutting cycle times 50%. Sustainability push: 70% of alts now Paris-aligned, including green bonds and impact PE.

Overall, our portfolio yielded 5.6% year-to-date (pre-fees), with Sharpe ratio of 1.2—top-quartile versus AM Best peers like MetLife and Lincoln National. Strategic shifts: de-risking by trimming equities by 1% into privates if 10Y yields breach 4.5%; full rollout of portfolio optimization engine using ML for scenario testing like 200bps rate shock; $15 billion dry powder for opportunistic buys in dislocated HY/EM debt; $20 billion equity put spreads and FX hedges for CAD/EUR exposures. Regionally, U.S. strength offsets Eurozone slowdowns, while Asia growth funds P&C expansion. Looking ahead, we expect 5.8-6.2% portfolio yield in H2, assuming Fed cuts twice, with alternatives driving outperformance. This allocation positions us for sustained ROE above 12%, funding 8% dividend growth and $2 billion buybacks.

Next, let's focus on one of our core profitability metrics: the combined ratio, both overall and by segment. For those new to our story, the combined ratio is the gold standard in property and casualty insurance, calculated as the sum of our loss ratio—incurred losses and loss adjustment expenses divided by earned premiums—and our expense ratio—underwriting, acquisition, and operational costs also over earned premiums. A combined ratio below 100% indicates underwriting profit, and we're proud to report continued discipline driving ours lower.

Our consolidated combined ratio for Q2 came in at 92.4%, reflecting the maturation of our multi-year pricing cycle, enhanced risk selection via our proprietary AI-driven underwriting platform—which we've rolled out across 85% of our book now—and disciplined expense management amid moderating inflation pressures. Excluding catastrophe losses, our adjusted combined ratio was an exceptional 87.5%, underscoring underlying profitability even before weather hits. Year-to-date through Q2, the combined ratio stands at 93.1%, down from 96.2% in the same period last year, positioning us ahead of the industry average of 97.8% as reported by ISO and AM Best data. This outperformance is driven by earned rate increases averaging 8.2% across our portfolio—with renewals at 9.5%—and a 15% reduction in large loss frequency due to our advanced telematics integration in personal auto.

By segment: Personal Lines (52% of net earned premiums, $4.2 billion in Q2): combined ratio 90.1%, improving 320 basis points year-over-year from 93.3%. Homeowners at 89.5%, benefiting from catastrophe modeling upgrades using third-party data from RMS and our in-house climate analytics, which allowed us to non-renew 12% of highest-risk coastal exposures in Florida and the Gulf Coast. Auto at 91.2%, with loss ratios dipping to 65.4% thanks to our DriveSafe telematics program, now with 2.8 million policyholders, delivering 22% reduction in claims severity. Expense ratio 24.7%, flat sequentially, as digital servicing via our app cut agent touchpoints by 18%.

Commercial Lines (32% of NEP, $2.6 billion): standout at 93.8%, down 180 basis points from 95.6% last year. Middle-market property at 92.4%, supported by 11.3% earned rate and shift toward preferred risks—we've grown workers' comp by 14% while exiting high-hazard construction classes. General liability saw pressure from social inflation, loss ratio 68.2%, but machine learning for reserve adequacy kept development favorable at -1.2 points. We've expanded cyber product suite, booking $180 million in premiums with 85% combined ratio.

Specialty and Reinsurance (16% of NEP, $1.3 billion): 91.2%, marginally up due to $45 million in cat losses from European floods, but ahead of Lloyd's 98% composite. Excess and surplus at 88.7%, fueled by 15.2% rate momentum. Reinsurance assumed book, retroceding 40% to Swiss Re, at 92.5%, with Asia-Pacific growth 22% offsetting Europe.

Regionally: U.S. (78%) at 92.0%, aided by California wildfire mitigation; EMEA at 95.4%, pressured by UK motor but strong Continental; Asia (8%) at 89.2% via parametric partnerships like Ping An. These affirm our Profitable Growth 2026 initiative: targeting sub-90% by year-end through AI claims triage slashing cycle times 35%, reinsurance optimization, and growing specialty to 20% while capping personal cat exposure at 15% of surplus. Tailwinds from +7% industry renewals per Verisk, tempered by La Niña.

As we discuss investments further, our investment income yield came in at 4.35% for the quarter on an annualized basis. This represents a 52 basis point improvement quarter-over-quarter and a robust 78 basis point increase year-over-year, significantly outperforming our statutory book yield target of 4.0% and driving $285 million in net investment income—up 12% from Q2 2023.

Calculated as net investment income, excluding trading gains or losses, divided by average carrying value of invested assets, with $145 billion total at quarter-end—primarily high-quality fixed income—this metric underscores strength on our $112 billion float growing at 5% CAGR. Fixed income (72%) delivered 4.65%, up from 3.92% YoY, via duration extension to 5.8 years from 5.2, locking 5.1% on 10-year IG corporates. Deployed $8.2 billion new: 45% NAIC 1 munis at 4.2% tax-equivalent, 30% agency MBS at 4.8%, 15% IG corporates like JPMorgan.

Credit quality: 92% NAIC 1/2, 3% HY at 7.2% via energy transition. Equities/alts (15%/13%) blended 3.8%; equity 4.1% via dividend aristocrats like J&J; alts 6.5% from Blackstone/Starwood. Regional: U.S. 68% (Treasuries 4.6%), Europe 20% (4.2% USD-equivalent), Asia 12% (4.7% AUD/SGD). ALM layered $4.5 billion swaps; ESG 28% new commitments; Aladdin for scenarios. Ahead of Prudential (4.1%), MetLife (4.0%); guide 4.4-4.6% FY.

Before moving on, let's unpack realized and unrealized gains and losses, contributing $180 million pre-tax. Portfolio $152 billion, up 4% YoY; alloc 72% fixed, 18% equities, 7% alts, 3% cash. Book yield 3.8%, new money 4.6%.

Realized: $285 million net gains, up 45% YoY/$210M Q1. Harvested $120M corporates rotation (Verizon/AT&T); $95M equities (KBW Bank, JPM/BRK); $70M alts (1.4x direct lending). Losses $25M MBS. Realized yield 2.9% TTM > peers.

Unrealized: $420M net loss, narrowing YoY/Q1; accum OCI -$4.2B (2.8%). Duration 5.2yrs hit by +25bps Agg to 4.85% ($350M fixed losses); munis $80M. Gains: equities $120M (S&P +5%, Tech/HC); alts $35M (IRA infra/CLO). ALM: duration mismatch to 0.4yrs via $5B swaps; shift to 12% structured credit (Blackstone/Apollo 7-9% IRR); ESG 28% green. Guide $200-250M Q realized; FY income $1.0-1.2B.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial lines segment. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including expanded use of AI in pricing and telematics for auto.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for questions: press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from John Ramirez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the reinsurance recoveries outlook and how it impacts your combined ratio guidance?

Michael Reynolds: Good morning, John. Absolutely. As David detailed, our $650-700 million full-year recoveries guide, with strong H2 inflows, directly supports our net loss ratios and the 92.4% Q2 combined. We've baked in normalized cats, and the favorable development from Idalia and wildfires gives us confidence in sustaining sub-93% YTD, positioning for sub-90% ex-cat as pricing cycles mature.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of rising rates on your asset allocation and investment yield?

David Chen: Good morning, Emily. The higher-for-longer environment has been tailwind, with our 4.35% yield reflecting duration extension and selective credit picks. Fixed income at 72% yielded 4.65%, and we're tactically increasing alts to 13% for 7-9% IRRs. If rates hold, we see 4.4-4.6% FY, with ALM hedges keeping duration matched and capital resilient at 520% RBC.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee: Good morning. What is the expected impact of regulatory changes around ESG reporting on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Tom. ESG regs like SFDR and NAIC updates are integrated into our models already—60% IG ESG-compliant, 70% alts Paris-aligned. For underwriting, it enhances risk selection in climate-exposed lines, like non-renewing high-risk coasts, and opens parametric growth in Asia. No material drag; it's a competitive edge aligning with specialty expansion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: Thanks. On unrealized losses—how sensitive is your OCI to further rate hikes, and any changes to realized gains strategy?

David Chen: Rachel, good question. Unrealized at -$4.2B is manageable at 2.8% of fair value, with hedges covering 60% rate sensitivity. A 25bps rise like Q2 costs ~$350M; we're stress-tested to 200bps shocks. Realized gains moderate to $200-250M/quarter as we prioritize yield over harvesting, rotating into 5-7% corporates.

Operator: Thank you. That concludes the question queue. I'll now turn it back to the company for closing remarks.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Unity Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
